articleTitle: Design of circular patch antennas for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze the design of a circular patch antenna at 28 GHz band for 5G applications. Our objective is to design and simulate circular patch antenna using coaxial feed microstrip line feed and compare their performance. The antennas are designed using RT/Duroid 5880 substrate material. The performance of the coaxial feed circular antenna is better than the linefeed circular antenna. The bandwidth of the coaxial fed antenna is 0.792 GHz while the bandwidth of the microstrip line fed antenna is 0.660 GHz.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based 2-DoF-PID power system stabilizer design for damping out low frequency oscillations in power systems
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Low frequency oscillation (LOF) could be a serious concern in grid. It may occur due to tiny signal perturbation. It will cause complete grid collapse. Power system stabilizer (PSS) is used to help the system by rising the damping of grid. During this paper, particle swarm optimization (PSO) based two-degree of freedom PID stabilizer is planned to enhance the damping of the system. The stabilizer parameters are tuned utilizing PSO. Integral square error (ISE) is picked as the objective criterion for the plan. To execute this, IEEE type DC1 exciter with single machine unbounded bus (SMUB) system is considered. The execution of the PSO based 2-DoF-PID is compared with PSO based PI, PID stabilizers. To check the viability of the structured stabilizers, comparatives investigation is finished with some current outcomes.

articleTitle: Glottal Signal Analysis for Voice Pathology
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The work present in this paper is focusing on a method for the detection of voice disorders related to the pathologies of vocal folds. It extracts glottal signal parameters by using inverse filtering method. Support Vector Machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighboring (k-NN) classifiers are used for differentiating healthy and non-healthy persons. The voice samples of the person belonging to both the categories were acquired using a specialized voice recorder. SVM provided 98.5 % whereas k-NN provided 88.2 % accuracy. Voice signals of patients affected with vocal cord nodules were also collected and tested with same classifier. The Accuracy of 78.9 % and 70.4% were obtained with SVM and k-NN respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power and High Speed XOR/XNOR Circuit using 90 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, a high speed and low power XOR-XNOR circuit in hybrid logic style in 90 nm CMOS technology is presented. The proposed XOR-XNOR circuit is symmetrical and has only single pass transistor in all delay paths. The designed circuit provides simultaneous generation of XOR-XNOR logic, balanced output and exhibits full voltage swing in all internal and external nodes. Due to full swing in delay path, the circuit has high portability, high noise robustness, and good driving capabilities. The simulation results show 8%, 5%, and 13.2% improvement in delay, power consumption and Power Delay Product (PDP), respectively. The circuit has used only 10 transistors.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation using K-means Clustering and Deep Learning in Satellite Image
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning based method, aided by certain clustering algorithm for use in semantic segmentation of satellite images in complex background is proposed. The work considers the formation and training of SegNet in which the output of K-means clustering algorithm is used as input and the label of the particular region of interest (ROI) in the image are used as target. The method does not require any feature extraction, region growing or splitting methods to configure and train the SegNet, which is a deep convolutional Encoder-Decoder architecture trained with (error) Back Propagation learning. The method is tested with different satellite images. The method is also compared with the results obtained when trained with SegNet without selecting the ROI using K-means algorithm and evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, mean IoU and weighted IoU. The normalized confusion matrix is also plotted. The experimental results show that the method is reliable and suitable for real world situations.

articleTitle: Design of Memristor – CMOS based logic gates and logic circuits
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Recent researches are mostly focused on technology scaling as well as device size minimization design techniques following Moore’s law. Conventional computing architectures are unable to fulfill modern application demands. Memristor is a promising alternative device which has been developed by many researchers [2] to draw attention of its structure for numerous applications which includes computational logic, memory implementations and neuromorphic systems. This paper emphasizes the basic properties of memristor at the device level. Different digital circuits have been designed for logic operations and DSP applications. Design methodologies are developed for proper circuit design, and circuit parameters are taken from a very detailed device model and optimization techniques. The transient response of Hybrid CMOS-memristor based logic gates and different adder circuits (i.e, half adder, full adder, carry-save adder) and multiplier circuit are performed in Cadence 180nm technology.

articleTitle: A Ditherless 2.4GHz High Resolution LC DCO
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper presents an LC-based digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) with an enhanced frequency resolution. Tuning range of the circuit is 2.2GHz to 2.98GHz with a fine resolution of 100Hz. The DCO exhibits a phase noise of -115.3 dBc/Hz at 1MHz frequency offset and a Figure of Merit (FoM) of -181 dBc/Hz. The circuit consumes 1.25mA current and designed with 65-nm eight-metal CMOS technology with an operating supply voltage of 1.0 V.

articleTitle: Smart Grid:Cyber Attack Identification And Recovery Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Although smart grid concept helps existing grid to achieve maximum benefits but security concern about how to identify malicious and how to recover in stipulated time is major concern. The malignant threads due to cyber-attack will impact the reliability of the system. Smart grid concept is totally relying on the communication network using Internet Protocols (IP) based system for its fast response making it expose to different vulnerability. This paper deals with malicious cyber-attack identification and possible recovery methods for smart grid.

articleTitle: Real–Time Yoga Activity with Assistance of Embedded based Smart Yoga Mat
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Yoga is a predominating approach to dissolve the physical diseases and reduce stress. A Yoga mat plays a vital role in performing yoga, in this regard, there is a need of Smart Yoga Mat to assist the human postures and to provide the Biofeedback to the subject (human). This paper proposes a novel Embedded based Smart Yoga Mat (ESYM) design and its implementation. In this work, initially the pressure nodes are identified on ESYM and from that nodes pattern is generated using FSR sensors. An algorithm for the pattern identification has been developed to evaluate Yoga postures. The posture correction of subjects is provided in real time with Biofeedback mechanism. The experimental setup is developed with NI-myRIO as the control unit of ESYM and a mat with the pressure sensors. The coding is done using LabVIEW software. The developed Prototype is validated by conducting experiments on subjects for the sitting and lying yoga postures.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Solar-Wind Energy In ELD with Thermal Units by Adaptive Jaya Algorithm for Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, wind-solar generation has been included in the ELD with thermal units. Here ELD incorporating wind-solar energy has been done for thermal units. There are some thermal generating units, solar power generating unit and wind power generating unit. Each thermal unit has upper bound and lower bound. Adaptive Jaya Optimization Technique has been utilized here to get the better solution or optimal generation for ELD in the environment of Matlab. Minimum power generating cost has to make out after including the wind generation and solar generation. Here this result is showing the minimum cost of Adaptive Jaya Optimization Technique than the other evolution method. Incorporation of solar-wind in ELD for thermal units with the help of Adaptive Jaya algorithm has been done in this current work.

articleTitle: Critical Dimension of Word2Vec
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Word embeddings are an efficient way of representing text such that they can be used by different Machine Learning Algorithms. Word2Vec is one such word embedding model. Although it is highly efficient, this model can take up a lot of space to store the vector representations. So defining the appropriate dimension of this model is very important to improve its performance in memory restricted devices. In this work, we present an empirical approach to decide the dimension of the word embeddings for a specific set of documents (corpora) to a critical value such that the representation of the words still preserve their original semantic and syntactic meanings. In this context, principal component analysis (PCA) has been used to compare the precision of vectors represented in different dimensions.

articleTitle: Joint Source Channel Coding with MIMO MC-CDMA for Efficient Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The inclusion of joint source and channel coding (JSCC) in the same processing block decreases the system complexity and reduces the cost and overall processing period as compared to the use of separate source and channel coding techniques. The perfect combination of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) with code division multiple access (CDMA) that yields multi carrier (MC)-CDMA (MC-CDMA) can increase the channel capacity with the division of available bandwidth into many narrow bands. Multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) technology is known to improve the capacity and throughput significantly of wireless systems. In this paper, we analyze the performance of MC-CDMA techniques with JSCC in 2*2 MIMO set-up which reduce the data loss during recovery and increase the channel capacity. Lossless data compression and reliable data delivery are the aims of JSCC with greater link reliability and better capacity. We combine JSCC and Fountain coding together with MC-CDMA and deploy it over a MIMO arrangement to see the performance difference. The primary objective of our system with JSCC, MC-CDMA and MIMO is to reduce the system complexity, obtain better link reliability with higher gain in capacity.

articleTitle: A full-duplex pilot-assisted DP-16-QAM CO-OFDM system for high-speed long-haul communication
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: A full-duplex coherent transceiver system is presented for high-speed long-haul communication. Coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) along with dual-polarization 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (DP-16-QAM) scheme has been implemented to achieve a data rate of 320 Gbps for both the downlink and uplink. Training symbols are used for channel estimation and a maximum transmission distance of 600 km of single-mode fiber (SMF) is achieved with comb-type pilot carriers for carrier phase estimation (CPE). The OFDM and inphase-quadrature modulator (IQM) structure can be fabricated in the form of low-cost integrated circuits (ICs) and the system possesses high reliability towards spectrally-efficient broadband communication. The overall system performance is evaluated considering bit error rate (BER) for maximum data rate, transmission distance and receiver sensitivity.

articleTitle: Nonidentical Chaotic Secure Communication Using Proportional Integral Sliding Mode Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper puts forward a secure communication scheme based on synchronisation between nonidentical (topologically non-equivalent) chaotic systems using sliding mode control (SMC) technique. A drive-response philosophy is used where one chaotic system is known as a transmitter and other chaotic system with controller is termed as a receiver. Lu chaotic system is considered as a drive system and Bhalekar-Gejji (BG) chaotic system is considered as a response system. Proportional integral (PI) sliding surfaces are designed to achieve synchronisation between nonidentical chaotic systems to achieve secure communication. Sliding mode control law is designed to ensure the system trajectories to the designed sliding surfaces. Required asymptotic stability condition is derived using Lyapunov stability theory. MATLAB simulation environment is used for numerical simulation of the proposed communication scheme. Simulation results reveal the successful achievement of the proposed nonidentical chaotic systems synchronisation based concept to secure communication.

articleTitle: Secure and Composite Routing Strategy through Clustering In WSN
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Due to openness of the deployed environment and transmission medium, Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) suffers from various types of security attacks including Denial of service, Sinkhole, Tampering etc. Securing WSN is achieved a greater research interest and this paper proposes a new secure routing strategy for WSNs based on trust model. In this model, initially the sensor nodes of the network are formulated as clusters. Further a trust evaluation mechanism was accomplished for every sensor node at Cluster Head level to build a secure route for data transmission from sensor node to base station. Here the trust evaluation is carried out only at cluster head and also the cluster head is chosen in such a way the node having rich resources availability. The trust evaluation is a composition of the social trust and data trust. Simulation experiments are conducted over the proposed approach and the performance is measured through the performance metrics such as network lifetime, and Malicious Detection Rate. The obtained performance metrics shows the outstanding performance of proposed approach even in the increased malicious behavior of network.

articleTitle: H∞ Performance based Robust State Feedback Controller design for Interconnected Power system with Delay
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance based robust state feedback controller design scheme is proposed for interconnected power system (IPS) with time delay. A linear matrix inequality (LMI) based robust stabilization criterion is derived by constructing suitable Lyapunov-Krasovskii (LK) functional in order to get better control performance. At last, an uncertain two-area power system containing time-delays in area control error (ACE) signals is considered as an example to illustrate the effectiveness and usefulness of the state feedback controller.

articleTitle: A review on artifacts removal techniques for Electroencephalogram signals
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is used for the diagnosis of brain disorders (like epilepsy, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) etc). Artifacts are the unwanted interference in the EEG signal because of eye movements, blinks, muscle activity, heartbeats, power line noise etc. Different techniques were proposed to get artifacts free EEG signal for improving the accuracy while doing feature extraction and data classification. In this paper, conventional methods for noise removal are described and recent techniques are reviewed.

articleTitle: Wideband Triangular Patch Antenna for Cognitive Radio in TV White Space
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna design is proposed for use in Cognitive Radio (CR) applications in the TV white Space (TVWS) frequency range (470-806 MHz). The situation of TVWS in India is discussed along with the needs for spectrum sensing through wideband antenna for CR application. A triangular patch is considered as a base design. Then, to achieve the desired bandwidth of TVWS, loading of meander line and passive triangular ring is performed which excites additional resonances adjacent to main resonance. This results in the enhancement of the antenna bandwidth. The results and other parameters are further discussed for an in depth analysis of the designed antenna. The obtained results confirm the usability of the designed antenna for TVWS communication.

articleTitle: Nano-sized Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna for X Band Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Recent researches have extensively explored patch antenna design for deriving better performance for operation in X band. One of the novel techniques in slotted microstrip patch antenna design is to cut nano-sized slots over the substrate of the patch. Nanostructures are expected to provide unique characteristics and can possibly help in performance improvement of the patch antenna. This paper focuses on the study and design of a rectangular slotted microstrip patch antenna in High Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS) simulation software for X band operation. The antenna is designed over an RT Duroid 5880 substrate with 100nm×100nm dimension square slots over its surface. The square slots are arranged in five different forms and their performances are compared. The results show that there is an improvement in the return loss with an increasing number of slots.

articleTitle: RF parameter extraction and S-parameter analysis of junctionless silicon nanowire transistor
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, RF and S-parameters analysis of Junc-tionless Silicon Nanowire (JLSNW) Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field-effect-transistor (MOSFET) are presented. The small-signal parameters such as source to drain capacitance, transconductance and total gate input capacitance etc. are extracted and comparisons are performed with conventional silicon nanowire MOSFET parameters. A Non-quasi-static RF model is used for validation of extracted parameters through S-parameter analysis for the first time. The device is also evaluated for various RF parameters such as cut-off frequency, transport time delay and maximum oscillation frequency. The simulated and mathematically calculated values of these parameters are showing approximate similar results up to the high-frequency of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>.

articleTitle: A comparison study of on-chip and optimized gate inductor of an LNA
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In a receiver frontend, LNA (Low noise amplifier) is an essential block to amplify required low power signal buried under noise. According to Frii’s formula Noise Factor of the transceiver primarily depends on the NF (Noise Figure) & gain of first RF component i.e. LNA. Traditionally, the most critical design parameter of LNA belongs to input matching and low noise figure. Subsequently, it has been observed that, design of CMOS based LNA design critically depends on inductors present in the design. In present paper a comparative study has been done between on-chip inductor and optimized gate inductor based LNA. This is validated in Cadence Virtuoso Tool using TSMC 180 nano-meter technology CMOS process with power supply of 1.8 volts. Approach for design of narrow band cascaded and cascoded Low Noise Amplifier with inductor source degenerated technique is used at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: A Non-intrusive Opto-mechanical Technique for the Measurement of Liquid Level
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an opto-mechanical technique suitable for measurement of liquid level with a very high resolution. In the propose technique, the change in the liquid level in the cylindrical container, attached to the bottom of a vertically suspended helical extension spring, causes corresponding change in the elongation length of the spring. The change in the elongation length eventually changes the distance between a diverging light source and a photoresistor. The repeated experimental observations show that the proposed technique has good resolution, very small non-linearity, high repeatability and negligible hysteresis error.

articleTitle: Emotion recognition from EEG signals using back propagation neural network
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The proposed work presents a discrete wavelet based feature extraction method in conjunction with a back propagation neural network (BPNN) for the classification of emotions from EEG recordings. The EEG recordings were used from DEAP dataset (A Database for emotion analysis using physiological signals) for evaluation of the method. Russell’s model was used for quantification of emotions in valence and arousal dimension space. The emotions were classified into four classes, namely – high arousal positive valence (HAPV), high arousal negative valence (HANV), low arousal positive valence (LAPV) and low arousal negative valence (LANV). We have used three mother wavelets Sym8, Coif5 and Db8 for extracting four features, namely entropy, mean, standard deviation and variance. Classification of the emotions was done using BPNN. An average classification accuracy of 57.9% was obtained in the classification of the above mentioned four classes using different mother wavelets.

articleTitle: Modeling a H-H Neuron based Spiking Neural Network incorporating Multiple Pre-synaptic Inputs
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) is the latest generation of Artificial Neural Networks that draws strength from the capability to closely mimic its biological counterpart. The choice of the spiking neuron that constitutes the core entity of a SNN determines its effectiveness for a particular application. Certain situations such as "neuron replacement therapy" can demand a precise realization of the biological neural net by the bio-mimetic prosthesis. Such specific prerequisites can only be catered using a network comprising of detailed neuron models that encompasses synaptic interactions between multiple neurons. Hence, in the proposed work, a simple spiking neural network is modeled using a "conjoint" neuron model that amalgamates the strengths and versatilities of the H-H model, Integrate-and-Fire model and Synapse model and thus presents a unique representation of the membrane behaviour due to multiple temporally varying and spatially distributed synaptic inputs.

articleTitle: A Novel Structure of Double-Gate Tunnel FET with Extended Back Gate for Improved Device Performances
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this brief, we have investigated a novel structure of double-gate TFET with extended back gate (EBG-DG-TFET) to improve the device performances. In the proposed device, the extended back gate is found to create an overlapped region with both source side as well as drain side which improves the overall performances of DG-TFET. Through two-dimensional numerical simulations, it is demonstrated that the overlapped gate-source region enhances the ON-state current due to reduction in the barrier width at input tunneling interface between source and channel regions, thus improving the current switching ratio of DG-TFET. In addition to improvement in ON-state current, the overlapped gate-source region also improves the subthreshold slope which is found to be lower than that of the conventional DG-TFET. Furthermore, the overlapped gate-drain region is found to remove the ambipolar conduction in DG-TFET when gate is biased with opposite polarity than drain terminal.

articleTitle: Modelling Signal Transmission in Passive Dendritic Fibre Using Discretized Cable Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Signal transmission and propagation in neuronal fibres is one of the complex and fascinating process that leads to varied dendritic signal dynamics depending on the complexity of the dendritic arbour. Such process of individual fibres can be modelled with the cable equation and passive cable representation. In the proposed work, emphasis is given in modelling of such individual dendritic fibre, since such dendritic arbour might affect the neuronal dynamics by a varied range. Hence, an attempt is made to model the signal propagation in passive dendritic fibre, considering the length and diameter dependence instead of length constants and time constants of the fibre. Considering the electrical equivalent cable model, the differential equation for passive fibre dynamics is modelled. Further, in order to incorporate the length and diameter of the fibre into the model, the modelled equation is discretized assuming the passive fibre to be linear. The results of the modelled equation shows that the propagation loss in a uniform cable minimizes with increase in the diameter thus describing the cause of losses in thin distal dendritic branches whereas the propagation losses increases with increasing length describes the successful transmission as a cumulative sum of signals in the primary dendritic branches connected directly to the soma.

articleTitle: Real Time Detection and Tracking of a Model Car using Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper elucidates a procedure for real time detection and tracking of a moving model car in the sequence of image frames acquired by a static camera. The vehicle tracking is performed by exploiting the modelling behavior of Kalman filter. The raw image acquisition, background subtraction, detection of vehicle in image frames is performed using image processing techniques. The vehicle tracking is performed by employing the modelling efficiency of a traditional Kalman filter. The raw image acquisition, background subtraction, to detect vehicle in image frames is performed using image processing techniques. The vehicle parameter estimation is further performed using the Kalman filter. This system takes raw image of two dimensional (2D) drivable surface with car as input, and outputs the spatial coordinates of estimated car position. The system was implemented on a ‘VEEROBOT’ robotic car in the laboratory environment. Real time images were taken using a ‘Logitech’ webcam, and the relevant processing is carried out using ‘Raspberry pi 3’. The analysis of experimental results between the measured and estimated position of the car is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: An approach to design memristive biosensor by using Zinc Oxide nanosample
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The work signifies the direct biosensing of E. coli bacteria using a memristor mode of nano device using ZnO (Zinc Oxide) quantum dots. These ZnO quantum dots are synthesized by aqueous precipitation method. The obtained nanoparticles have been characterized by UV- visible spectroscopy (UV), X-ray diffraction(XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM).The size and shape confirms the nano structure. Zinc oxide nanoparticles are known for their various applications in bio imaging. E.coli bacteria are conjugated to these nanosamples and finally these bacteria is sensed on dried samples based on memristive property. Varying the concentration of bacteria shows a variation of currents which follows a hysteresis pattern.

articleTitle: A study of Spoken Word Recognition using Unsupervised Learning with reference to Assamese Language
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to measure the performance of Auto Associative Neural Network (AANN) in terms of recognition rate of spoken words with reference to Assamese language. One AANN models is built in the present study for spoken word recognition using continuous speech database. The recognition is measured by taking Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) as the feature vector along with its first and second derivatives. In this study, one database is created by using continuous speech. In the continuous database, there are 240 continuous speech files each around two minutes of duration to train and test the AANN model. AANN is trained using the continuous speech database and the recognition of certain words present within the continuous speech signal is measured. In this study, fifteen native Assamese speakers are used which involves eight male speakers and seven female speakers. It is observed that the performance of AANN is 85.08% in terms of accuracy and the performance of AANN is 93.61% in terms of sensitivity.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Vibration Measurement based on FM demodulation in PLL Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, vibration measurement system is proposed by applying F M demodulation technique in phase-locked loop (PLL). The PLL block is designed by combining four units; comb-resonator unit, low pass filter unit, controller unit and sampling pulse generator unit. The cascading comb-resonator structure is derived from the standard sliding-discrete Fourier transform (SDFT) by introducing Goertzel algorithm. The high frequency carrier signal of 40kHz can be used to sense the Doppler signal and correspondingly the vibration parameters; amplitude and frequency, are estimated from extracted Doppler signal. The proposed system could estimate the vibration parameters with reduced computation complexity by removing the twiddle factor term in the recurring part of the system function. A stable system is assured by introducing a damping factor in the system function that allows the pole to shift within or on the unity circle of z −plane. A wide range of vibration amplitude and frequency can be estimated with less error. Effect of input noise can be suppressed up to small values of SNR.

articleTitle: Performance Degradation in Wireless Mesh Networks via External and Internal Attacks
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Wireless Mesh Networks (WMNs) upraised as superior technology offering all aspects of services as personal networking, social networking, and neighborhood networking. Due to its distributed nature and multi-hop environment, a centralized authentication scheme is not applicable in WMNs. Therefore, WMNs suffers from both external and internal attacks which could decrease the overall performance of WMNs. In the past various approaches had proposed to overcome such attacks to improve network performance and offering an uninterrupted service to the end-users. This paper presents a detailed investigation of various security techniques that had proposed so far and made a comparison based on their performance against external and internal attacks in WMNs.

articleTitle: An idea of implementing CMOS operational amplifier in summer configuration for the designing of highly sensitive pressure transducer
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This work presents the designing and simulation of a piezoresistive pressure transducer using an operational amplifier (op-amp) in summer configuration for higher pressure sensitivity. Piezoresistors placed on high-stress regions of the square silicon diaphragm are used as the sensing elements that detect the variation in the resistance of piezoresistors under an applied pressure range of 0-1 MPa in a step size of 100 KPa. An operational amplifier circuit has been designed using five micron CMOS technology parameters in T-Spice simulation tool. A non-inverting op-amp in summer configuration has been used as the readout circuit of the pressure transducer which converts the resistance variation of piezoresistors into output voltage. The Intellisuite software has been used to simulate the analytical model which describes the complete behavior of the pressure transducer employing both p-type and n-type piezoresistors as the sensing elements. Simulation result clearly shows that the op-amp in summer configuration based pressure transducer using p-type and n-type piezoresistors have a sensitivity of 187 mV/MPa and 1047 mV/MPa, respectively.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Carrier Depletion based P-N junction Optical Phase Shifter using Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The mathematical modeling of PN junction optical phase shifter has been done for electrical and optical domain characteristics and respective graphs have been shown. NSGA-II based MOGA has been applied to optimize change in optical properties (∆n and ∆α) with respect to change in electrical properties (∆Ne and ∆Nh ) of PN junction before characterizing the device. The values obtains are ∆n= -3.5x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, ∆α= 12.74 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for ∆Ne= 1.19x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and ∆Nh = 4.30x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The results of mode profile, carrier distribution, and small signal response in terms of cut-off frequency, loss = 9.6 dB/cm at reverse bias condition of PN junction in depletion mode give sufficient insight into the device for the use of Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) based Optical Fiber Communication (OFC)System. Interconnection problem between silicon integrated chips and the outside world is taking care of by using a coupler.

articleTitle: Low Phase Noise 2.45GHz LC VCO Based On Current Reuse Technique in 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Phase noise always played a critical role while designing a Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO). In this literature a new architecture of low phase noise design is presented. current reusing technique has been employed by cross coupling both NMOS and PMOS structure. Moreover, the LC tank of the VCO consist of two PMOS inverse varactor along with an NMOS inverse varactor in order to reduce the phase noise. The circuit has been implemented in TSMC 180nm technology and operating at 2.45GHz. Obtained phase noise is of the order -123dBc/Hz@1MHz and -80dBc/Hz@100Hz.

articleTitle: DRV Evaluation of 6T SRAM Cell Using 45nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: We have evaluated Data Retention Voltage (DRV), an important characteristic of 6T SRAM cell in hold mode, for various process corners (PCs) by varying temperature (T). We noticed significant variation in the DRV value of 6T SRAM cell in hold mode for various PCs, Typical-Typical (TT), Slow-Slow (SS), Slow-Fast (SF), Fast-Slow (FS), Fast-Fast (FF) and Monte-Carlo (MC) at T= 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C, 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C, 50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C, 75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C and 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C. The highest DRV value obtained for FS process corner is 113.5 mV at 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C, 111 mV at 50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C, 108.5 mV at 75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C and 107 mV at 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C respectively. These values are considered as the worst case DRV. While for SS process corner the worst case DRV is reported as 120 mV at 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C temperature.

articleTitle: Physical model for drift in carbon nanotube based ZrO2 gate dielectric ion sensitive field effect transistor
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, a physical model for the drift behavior of carbon nanotube based ion sensitive field effect transistor (CNTISFET) with high-κ dielectric material ZrO2 as gate oxide is presented. Drift has been modeled as the threshold voltage instability with time based on hopping transport mechanism, also known as the dispersive transport. The exposure of ZrO2 surface to electrolyte solution leads to chemical modification of the surface and the resultant capacitance of the insulator changes with time. Thus, the threshold voltage of the device varies with time. The model has been verified with experimental drift characteristic results and a good fit was obtained.

articleTitle: Singer Identification Using Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Singer identification (SID) is the process of recognizing a singer by retrieving audio information from a particular song or segment of a song (if there is more than one singer). It is one of the most crucial applications of Music Information Retrieval (MIR) which use is becoming increasingly popular day by day. This paper proposes a method to identify singers from an available DAMP-balanced dataset using wavelet transform as a pre-processing step with Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) as the audio feature and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) as the classifier. The results in terms of classification accuracy and computation time are compared with and without using wavelet transform.

articleTitle: Voltage Controlled Stimulator For Nerve Conduction Study
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Use of an appropriate stimulus is essential to acquire proper nerve conduction signal. This paper presents a voltage controlled stimulator that generates proper voltage to be applied over the skin for nerve conduction study (NCS). Unlike conventional stimulator, the designed stimulator is based on battery which is suitable for portable nerve study machines. The recording and signal processing involve signal conditioning circuit that consisting of filter and amplifier circuits. The conditioning circuit amplifies and filters low-level biomedical signal, usually, falls in mV. Experimental setup has been tested and demonstrated using real-time data collected in laboratory. The system is adaptable to the subjects with safety.

Author Keywords: compound muscle action potential and signal conditioning circuit

articleTitle: Hierarchical Segmentation of Entities in a Handwritten Document
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The increasing deceptive ways of counterfeiting handwritings have given rise to the field of study of handwriting. In this digital age, considering the amount of data generated and to be processed, there is a need of computer-based verification for handwritings. The system designed for such purpose works on the feature extraction at various levels of an input document. Most of the feature extraction methodologies and algorithms deliver a lower efficiency due to improper segmentation of the handwriting samples. Hence, there arises a need of a robust image segmentation preprocessing block. A handwritten document has three main key elements forming it i.e. the sentences forming the document, the words forming the sentences and the characters forming the words. These elements are an ocean of opportunities for feature extraction, which is possible by extracting them efficiently and with minimum misidentifications. Hence, the paper presents a novel idea of segmentation into various levels of the elements forming the handwritten document. The proposed method exploits the behavior of watershed algorithm in combination with a linearly programmed approach for reliable segmentation of the handwritten documents.

articleTitle: Speaker Independent Speech Recognition System for Paite Language using C# and Sql database in Visual Studio
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Speech Recognition System is a technique that involves the implementation of codes and logical operations to enable the system to recognize the Spoken words which after being recognized by the machine generate its response in a machine-readable form and perform the required actions as per the commands that are given by the input speech. In this paper, a speech recognition system for Paite Language is implemented using Microsoft Visual Studio C#. This system is based on Speaker Independent system. Visual Studio has an inbuilt Speech Recognition engine which provides the speech recognizer to recognize the user's speech and integrate it with the inbuilt simulator. The System consists of a user interface which displays all the detected and recognized words after giving an Input Speech. It also has the facility to store more words to the Grammar by taking input from the user in the form of text. This can only be done by authenticated users. Unauthenticated users must first register themselves to add more phrases. Authenticated users then can utter their usernames and passwords in order to log in. If the matching usernames and passwords are found in the database, then only they will be directed to the page that allows users to add more words. 100 words in Paite Language were tested using the microphone. The result after calculating with confusion matrix gives an overall accuracy of 97.06%.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Carrier Injection based PIN junction Optical Phase Shifter using Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, with the help of 2D Drift-Diffusion equations, Maxwell’s wave equations and using evolutionary algorithm (MOGA), PIN and MOS based optical phase shifter are designed with optimum values of carrier concentrations 1.02×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> × and 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> of n and p region. The finite element method (FEM), finite difference method (FDM) and bisection method (BM) have been applied for simulation and calculations purpose. These results are useful for the design of PIN and MOS based optical modulator, either in Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) or microring resonator (MRR) configurations.

articleTitle: A Framework For Human Behaviour Detection Using Combined Analysis of Facial Expression and Eye Gaze
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Facial appearances like a happy, sad, disgust, surprise, angry, fear and Eye Gaze Estimations are the fastest means of communication while conveying any type of information. Expressions not only expose the sensitivity or feelings of any person but can also be used to judge his/her mental states. Therefore, it has become a wide interest area of research due to its applications to the fields like Human Computer Interface (HCI), Man Machine Interface (MMI) etc. In order to get more effective human behavior identification, we have presented a combination of facial expression recognition and eye gaze estimation technique where we have to recognize the real time expressions by using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with transfer learning method. After that, we determine the eye gaze by using Viola Jones, Circular Hough Transform (CHT) and a geometric method. With the combination of both processes, we able to predict the human behavior like drivers concentration levels. In this way experiments are carried out on MUG database for our own trained CNN model based on VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group) pre trained model and gives better performance with accuracy of 93% for training and 94% for overall process.

articleTitle: Development and characterization of Solid State RF amplifier for Heavy Ion Beam Buncher
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: A RF amplifier is of paramount importance to the successful operation of an ion beam bunching system. Solid state amplifier has lots of advantages over its vacuum tube counterparts, like compactness, reliability and modularity. In this paper we have discussed the development and characterization of a broadband 200W solid state amplifier. It has a power gain of 14 dB and power added efficiency of 60 %. The distortion due to most of the higher order harmonics is found to be less than –50 dBc.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Modified Global Routing Algorithm on a High-throughput Parallel Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Complexity and productivity of modern day Integrated Circuits (ICs) have increased due to aggressive transistor scaling. The exponential increase of circuit complexity brings a tremendous challenge to all phases in the design flow of ICs especially routing. Global routing is the most time consuming phase in physical design flow. As it needs to be performed multiple times, performance improvement in terms of time and solution is of prime importance. Several techniques have been developed including Rip-up and Reroute(RRR) and parallelization to achieve such goals. The work reported in this paper is executed on Julia which is configured for parallelism. Julia is a high-level, dynamic language with an easy-to-use multiprocessor mechanism and much less code complexity. Techniques proposed in this paper is implemented in Julia with an average 2x speed-up obtained on a quad-core processor compared to single core processing. Also, the proposed approach balances the load and reduces the overload on the processors.

articleTitle: Minimizing Vias and Wirelength in 3-D IC Floorplanning
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper proposes techniques for floorplanning in 3-D ICs. Although floorplanning has been extensively studied for last few decades. But increase in the scale of floorplanning instances, new architectures and ever evolving algorithms provides the motivation to incorporate new improved techniques to provide optimal solution. 3D ICs are better in performance compared to their 2-D representation because they occupy smaller die area, consume less power, have smaller wirelength and are lower in cost and hence perform better. In this paper we have proposed a heuristic based algorithm to reduce the Through Silicon Vias(TSVs) and Satisfiability Modulo Theories(SMT) driven floorplanning of the tiers. Our proposed work is successful in reducing the number of vias required in most of the GSRC and MCNC benchmarks benchmarks considerably. The proposed technique has given a good solution in terms of reduction in wirelength also.

articleTitle: Harmonic Extraction based on mHDFT Algorithm in PLL Techinique
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper proposes a harmonic extraction method based on modulated hopping DFT (mHDFT) in phase locked loop PLL technique. In presence of harmonics, a voltage or current signal can be deteriorated, and hence it is very much essential to extract harmonics from the signal to obtain a good power quality. The proposed PLL comprises of mHDFT filter, Phase Detector (PD), Moving Averager (MA), PI Controller and Numerically Controlled Oscillator (NCO). The mHDFT algorithm is introduced in PLL to reduce the computation burden by injecting time hopping technique in time series. It removes the instability due to the presence of twiddle factor term in the recursive path and also gives more accuracy as compared to other DFT algorithms. The proposed technique can extract the harmonic components of a signal in the presence of large noise. Mean Square Error (MSE) of the harmonic measurement approaches to the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB).

articleTitle: A Narrow Band Cascode Source Degeneration Low Noise Amplifier with π-Input Matching at 5 GHz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of the narrow band cascode source degeneration Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) operational at 5 GHz frequency. The LNA was designed with standard gpdk 180 nm technology using Cadence Virtuoso tool. In this paper, source degenerated inductor with cascode and current mirror configuration have been used. For the design of input and output matching circuits, π-match and L-match have been used respectively. Performance parameters like noise factor, S-parameters, gain, linearity etc. have been analysed for the proposed design. Various kinds of analysis like sp analysis, noise analysis, dc analysis, ac analysis and harmonic analysis have been performed for the validation of design. Analog Mixed Signal (AMS) CMOS process is utilized for the design of 5 GHz LNA. This LNA achieves source degeneration inductance feedback which is useful for low noise factor for 5GHz wireless applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual Band Antenna Using Square Closed Ring (SCR) Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Metasurface inspired superstrate are periodic structures where resonating metamaterial unit cells are arranged in a regular geometrical order. Recently, the metasurface antennas have attracted much attention due to the features of low profile, wide bandwidth, and easy implementation. In this paper a periodic Square Closed Ring (SCR) structure is proposed which is used to convert a single band microstrip antenna operating at 3.6 GHz to a dual band antenna system at 3.4 GHz and 5.5 GHz. Here, SCR is behaving as a periodic superstrate to enhance the radiation performance of the proposed antenna. The proposed structure shows significant improvement in the gain performance of the overall antenna system with a pick gain of 5.8dBi and 6.4dBi at 3.4 GHz and 5.5 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A Single Feed Circularly Polarized Array Antenna for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: A planar elliptical annular ring patch array antenna is reported. Two degenerate TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> modes are created by feeding the elliptical annular ring patch at an angle of −45° and +45° with respect to the major and minor axes of the ellipse. Thus, a good circular polarization is obtained by using a single feed point. A corporate feed structure is used for the excitation of the array elements. Simulation results show that the axial ratio is less than 3dB at the central frequency of 3.96GHz with a 3–dB axial ratio bandwidth of 7.5 MHz and broadside gain of 12.86dB.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity of Adaptive Transmission With MRC Receiver in Correlated η – μ Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Capacity analysis of Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC) diversity systems operating in correlated η −μ fading channels has been presented. A study on the effects of−correlation on the channel capacity has been performed. Different optimal and suboptimal adaptive systems are considered for the analysis. It has been obtained that with correlation the capacity of the system increases at higher SNR. This due to channels become good at higher SNR, and the high correlation signifies a similar kind of channel in all branches. The numerical and result sections provide a detailed study of the system.

articleTitle: Energy Detection over Dual Correlated Nakagami-m Fading Channels using Selection Diversity Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In Wireless Communications, Cognitive radio (CR) emerges as a boon to the mankind as it reduces the spectrum scarcity problem. Spectrum Sensing, the method to detect the presence or absence of licensed user is the fundamental problem of this system. This method employs different detection techniques in order to sense the radio environment simultaneously without interfering with the primary users. Energy Detection is the most popular among all the detection technique because of its low computational cost, easy implementation and less complexity. This technique is the most suitable for any environment since it does not require any knowledge of the primary user. In this paper, an analytical expression is derived for the corresponding average probability of detection over dual correlated Nakagami-m fading channel. The results suggest that the detection probability highly depends upon the severity of fading. This analytical expression is then verified using Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: A Compact 3rd Order SIW Filter with Improved Upper Band Performance for Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: In this paper, a compact 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order SIW direct coupled band pass filter which completely covers the Ku-Band is designed and simulated in HFSS. The higher frequency stop band performance of the filter is improved by using band-stop resonators on the top of the filter which eventually make it compact and radiation free unlike stubs and slots. The simulation results of the filter shows an insertion loss lower than 1 dB, the good upper stop band performance of the filter with return loss slightly above –10dB at 13GHz (–9.2dB) and at 18 GHz (–8.5dB) covering complete Ku-Band.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Multicore Erbium Doped Fiber Amplifier: Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The main aim of this study is to conduct the mode analysis of multicore erbium doped fiber amplifier (MC-EDFA) for different numbers of core, size and structure/arrangement of the core to observed different modes travel through multiple cores at wavelength within the range of 1525-1565nm. A comparative mode study is done among 3 cores, 5 cores and 7 cores MC-EDFA fiber using the simulated result under the same geometric condition in order to bring out which size, structure and numbers of cores are providing better results. Also normalized frequency has been calculated for different wavelength and various size of the core in order to discuss the characteristic and the patterns of modes and its effect on the number of modes traveling through the core.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Broadcast News Video Shot Segmentation and Classification
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Shot segmentation and categorization is one of the most important and primary steps in building efficient and well sorted video storage and retrieval system. News video story segmentation and commercial detection surely deserve special attention for creation of a well-categorized system as different types of news are being broadcast over a variety of news channels in television. However, in order to garner more viewers, different news channels use different spatial and temporal structures for broadcasting news. Keeping this approach in mind, we present an unsupervised method for shot detection, and subsequently, commercial and news shots are classified. The proposed method does not depend on different temporal and spatial structures adopted by different news channels, and our method needs significantly less number of manual parameters.

articleTitle: Moving Object Detection in Night Time: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The object monitoring performance is greatly depends on the enhanced quality of images. The quality of these images is affected at night video systems due to low contrast of salient objects as well as several atmospheric conditions such as fog, rain, dust etc. As a consequence, the intensity, color, polarization, coherence of scenes alters. The awful appearance of night images under subjective lighting and atmospheric conditions is a general problem for analysis in computer vision. In this paper, we have aimed to provide a survey work to researchers under four categories: (i) review on change detection datasets either thermal or visual-thermal, (ii) review on feature extraction based object detection techniques, (iii) review on background modeling based object detection techniques, (iv) review on convolutional neural network (CNN) based object detection techniques. This paper will benefits for those who require a details review over change detection datasets and detection techniques for moving object detection related applications.

articleTitle: Improved shuffled frog Leaping Algorithm for Path Planning of multiple Mobile-Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Improved shuffled frog leaping algorithm (ISFLA) has been proposed in this paper for multi-robot path planning in a clutter environment. Basic SFLA algorithm has been improved in the local search process by adding the weight and acceleration factor in the original version of SFLA to avoid the local optima and premature convergence. ISFLA technique has been embedded into the multi-robot system in a dynamic framework for generating optimal trajectory path by determining an optimal subsequent position for each robot from their existing position. Fitness function have been formulated by considering the different constraints and then, it optimized through ISFLA for generating optimal trajectory smooth path by avoiding the obstacles present in the environment. Finally, the simulation and experiment have been carried out to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The results obtained through ISFLA, SFLA and IGSA in terms of runtime, path deviation, the path travelled and energy utilized during travel shows ISFLA has outperformed its competitors.

articleTitle: A Remote Device Authentication Scheme for Secure Communication in Cloud Based IOT
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: The evolution of IOT that began with computers has now developed into an ecosystem. This IOT ecosystem consists of a large number of different types of devices embedded with sensors and technology, which makes them smart enough to interact within themselves. With IOT omnipresent, the challenge would be how to ensure only authorized access to the resulting smart system which in turn will ensure the security of the data gathered from these devices. In this paper, a very lightweight mutual authentication protocol based on Diffie Hellman for IOT enabled smart systems has been proposed. The proposed scheme possesses all the required security attributes and these attributes are validated by the widely accepted BAN logic.A thorough security analysis has been done to show that the proposed scheme is secure against different security attacks. The performance of the same has also been evaluated and compared with a number of existing methods. Performance analysis also demonstrates the effectivity of our proposed protocol.

articleTitle: Selection of an appropriate denoising technique for EEG signals of Parkinson’s disease patients
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Functions of human brain can be well analyzed by recording and analyzing the electrical activities of the brain. These analysis are very useful in providing accurate diagnosis and treatment of any disorders of this type. In the diagnosis of any neurological disorders, it is always necessary to give utmost importance to its methods of analysis. Despite poor spatial sensitivity compared to other methods of analysis of brain activities, EEG is used for this purpose because of its low cost recording machines, high temporal resolution etc.Although different works have been reported related to the diagnosis of epilepsy / Parkinson’s disease (PD), we have chosen the application of simple EEG comparison techniques for the purpose. We have taken samples of 10 numbers of subjects suffering from PD and 10 numbers of non PD persons. Prior to the extraction of any features for classification of these EEG signals, it is utmost important to preprocess them. This is necessary in order to remove the artifacts present in the signal considered for processing. In this paper, we are presenting an application of wavelet transforms (WT) by which the noise contained in the raw EEG of persons suffering from PD and of normal conditions can be reduced or eliminated with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Keyword Extraction using Graph Based Supervised Term Weighting
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Text classification of massive textual data has become an integral part and necessity of most computer applications. Eventually, term weighting becomes an important aspect as it directly affects the classification quality of document classification. The challenge of effective term weighting followed by the deficiency of traditional methods such as Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) method has encouraged numerous researchers to propose different algorithms. Term Frequency-Inverse Gravity Moment (TF-IGM) in vector space model is one such example which precisely measure the class distinguishing power of terms. In graph based model TextRank has become quite popular for term weighting. However, no algorithm has been proposed yet in graph based model which directly influences the class distinguishing power of a term. Hence, we propose a novel Graph Based Supervised Term Weighting (GBSTW) model which modifies the TextRank algorithm to incorporate class label information. The model has been validated using three mobile review data sets and has been compared with the pre-existing modified TextRank model. Results show that GBSTW model outperforms the pre-existing modified TextRank algorithm in terms of precision, recall and F-measure.

articleTitle: Parallel Multispectral Image Super-resolution Based on Sparse Representations
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Electronics, Signal Processing and Communication (IESC)
abstract: Image super-resolution (SR) produces a high-resolution (HR) image using either a single or multiple low-resolution (LR) input image(s) of the same scene. Sparse representation techniques are effectively applied for image SR because of their high reconstruction accuracy. SR reconstruction is accomplished through learning of an overcomplete dictionary and then solving a series of regularization problems applied on each patch extracted from the input image. This paper demonstrates a sparse representation based coupled overcomplete dictionary training and SR procedure for LR multispectral images. The proposed work is also implemented using a multicore parallel processing technique to provide faster reconstruction. Experimental results show superiority of the proposed method over some others.
